showcaseBenefit2Title: Built on experience with children, and on science
showcaseBenefit2Desc: The book and the Parent and Teacher Guide were written by an experienced mindfulness teacher and a teacher and researcher, weaving together our own experience with children and insights from research.

teacherHeroSub: A calm five minutes at the start of the day — narrated, ready to press play, and grounded in real nervous-system science, not one more thing to plan for.
teacherBenefit1Desc: Narrated sessions, calming activities, and discussion prompts already built — press play and the whole class settles together, no prep the night before.
teacherBenefit2Desc: Grounded in the FELT·FIBRE framework for nervous-system regulation — written by a meditation teacher and a child psychologist, not repackaged as another story app.
teacherBenefit3Desc: Lesson guides, printable handouts, and classroom tools in one place — sign in and new material shows up here as it's ready, no separate download each time.
teacherBelongingBody: Mare's classroom tools are still young, built alongside the teachers actually using them. What you ask for and what works in your room genuinely shapes what gets built next — not a suggestion box, a real conversation with the two people writing it.
teacherPeekSub: A few pages of what teachers get, open to everyone. Sign in for all of it.
teacherPeekPracticeLabel: From the Teacher's Guide · Chapter 1, The birthday party
teacherPeekPracticeTitle: Two practices, ready for tomorrow morning
teacherPeekPractice1Body: Before we do something difficult (answer a question, give a presentation, read something out to the class), we all press both heels firmly into the floor and breathe in and out slowly three times together – in through the nose, out through the mouth.
teacherPeekPractice2Body: Ask the children to think about a feeling of unease or nervousness that they sometimes experience. Encourage them to give it a funny, friendly name, such as ‘Charlie’, just for themselves. A name makes it easier to notice a feeling without getting carried away by it.
teacherPeekPracticeNote: Each of the book's 14 chapters has its own practices like these. Most take about a minute, and every one is something Mare does in the story.
teacherPeekScienceP1: Every child has a built-in alarm, present even before they are born, designed to keep them safe. Usually, it does its job well: it goes off when there is real danger and then switches itself off again.
teacherPeekScienceP2: For some children, however, that alarm doesn’t quite settle down. It can go off in response to everyday things – a loud noise, an unexpected change, a worrying thought – and struggles to calm down again on its own. This isn’t something a child can simply think their way out of. It requires gentle, repeated practice and time.
teacherPeekScienceP3: The good news is that this built-in brake gets stronger with practice, just like a muscle does. It doesn’t take any grand moments. It’s actually the small, everyday, repeated moments that count: a foot pressed firmly onto the floor, a slow breath, a hand feeling warmth, someone standing calmly beside you.
teacherPeekAuthors: Written by Dr Patricia Vuijk, primary school teacher, educational psychologist and academic researcher specialising in emotional safety and mindfulness, and Per Norrgren, mindfulness teacher and supervisor, clinician and founder of Deeper Mindfulness.
